doc.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Playing 'April in Paris' and a message to Hamilton students
summary: Grey plays 'April in Paris,' his most requested tune, and urges students to have the will to succeed, citing Basie's 'practice.'

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: We used to have to play this sometimes maybe three times a night, it was so asked for, the most requested tune that we had in the book, “April in Paris.” And all the students at Hamilton, I appreciate to have a few minutes to talk with you out there, and I want to let you know that this is a happy heart of finding out in the world that if you have a will, you can make it out there. And so Count Basie was that will that gave me all kinds of inspiration to be a pretty good artist today, and to do all the fills and things, many-a-times for Joe Williams, we have beautiful hearts, and I loved that band and everyone in that band, and so I have a lot to say today that if you have a will of wanting to play, I want you to get out there and come in with my idol, and he used to say “practice, practice, practice.” And I thank you for letting me have a moment with you. And you have been mighty wonderful, Mike, I thank you so much.
